reason: The text fragment (Genesis 27, the blessing of Jacob) does not support the statement. While Yahweh is briefly mentioned twice—once when Jacob attributes his hunting success to divine providence ('Yahweh your God caused it to happen'), and once when Isaac blesses Jacob with references to God's blessing of fields—the passage is primarily a narrative of family deception and patriarchal blessing. The text contains no discussion of Yahweh's attitudes toward 'Hebrew leaders' versus 'the people,' nor does it demonstrate Yahweh showing care for leaders while withholding empathy from people. The passage focuses on individual family members (Isaac, Jacob, Esau, Rebekah) rather than collective groups, and Yahweh's own actions, attitudes, or empathy toward either leaders or people are not addressed in this narrative.
